epochNote: Each row carries its own GP epoch (epochUTC, ISO-8601 UTC); there is no common epoch. GP rows (elementSource "celestrak-gp") are SGP4/SDP4 mean elements in the TEME frame and must be propagated with SGP4 (e.g. satellite.js json2satrec + propagate) from epochUTC to the display time; never use them as osculating Keplerian elements. Snapshot downloaded 2026-10-16T18:29:34.217Z to 2026-10-17T06:50:38.227Z (SATCAT 2026-10-15T20:56:28.000Z); median element age at retrieval 1.14 d, 95th percentile 3.67 d. SGP4 position error is ~1 km at epoch and typically grows by a few km per day in LEO (faster for low, high-drag objects); more than ~2 weeks from the epochs, positions should be presented as illustrative, and objects may have manoeuvred or re-entered since the snapshot. Rows with elementSource "satcat-shape" have no epoch: only perigee/apogee/inclination/period from SATCAT (render as reconstructed orbit shape with illustrative RAAN, argument of perigee and phase). Rows with elementSource null have no orbit information.
source: Orbital data: CelesTrak (celestrak.org) GP element sets and SATCAT, from U.S. Space Force 18th/19th SDS data via Space-Track.org.

units.norad: string (NORAD/USSF catalog number, decimal digits, up to 9; never a number)
units.epochUTC: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (GP EPOCH, microsecond precision, suffix Z)
units.meanMotionRevPerDay: rev/day (Kozai mean motion, SGP4 input MEAN_MOTION)
units.inclinationDeg: deg (TEME of epoch for GP rows; SATCAT value for satcat-shape rows)
units.raanDeg: deg (right ascension of ascending node, TEME of epoch)
units.bstar: 1/earth-radii (SGP4 B* drag term, earth radius 6378.135 km)
units.meanMotionDot: rev/day^2 (OMM MEAN_MOTION_DOT = first derivative of mean motion / 2, TLE convention)
units.meanMotionDdot: rev/day^3 (OMM MEAN_MOTION_DDOT = second derivative of mean motion / 6, TLE convention)
units.apogeeKm: km above a spherical Earth of radius 6378.135 km (mean apsis altitude)
units.perigeeKm: km above a spherical Earth of radius 6378.135 km (mean apsis altitude)
units.rcsM2: m^2 (radar cross-section as published in SATCAT)
